nodes.label: Phase 0a Follow-Ups — Execution Plan
nodes.rationale: Executes only the follow-ups that are self-contained and verifiable today; everything else stays on the standing to-do list with its reason intact. Deferrals are argued rather than listed: Approximate<T>'s first real consumer in Phase 3 decides its shape, and guessing now bakes in the wrong one.

nodes.label: Enterprise Layer
nodes.rationale: A layer variant above L3 holding lapidary-enterprise alone, named Enterprise rather than L4 because it is a wrapper tier existing for one product reason, not a fifth peer. L3 may not depend on it, protecting 'the application is free and complete'. Both crates were empty, so the change cost nothing then and gets more expensive with every file added.

nodes.label: Id Newtypes
nodes.rationale: LibraryId, PartId and RevisionId gain from_uuid and FromStr but deliberately not From<Uuid>: three distinct id types converting implicitly from one Uuid is exactly how a PartId ends up where a LibraryId belongs. lapidary-core may not depend on sqlx, so any Uuid-to-newtype query glue belongs in lapidary-db.

nodes.label: mock-kernel feature
nodes.rationale: The worker binary depends on lapidary-cad directly rather than through a feature chain via lapidary-api — the only option compatible with dropping the unused api -> cad edge, and it keeps the kernel out of the crate serving the open path. A startup log line reporting the linked kernel is a deliberate minimal real use; an unused optional dependency would repeat the mistake being removed.

nodes.label: publish = false
nodes.rationale: Internal path dependencies carried version = "0.1.0" only to satisfy deny.toml's wildcards = "deny", coupling eleven lines to the workspace version. publish = false on every application crate removes the coupling and prevents an accidental cargo publish of an AGPL app crate; allow-wildcard-paths = true is safe precisely because of it, and the two changes must never be separated.

nodes.label: Database Error Classification
nodes.rationale: connect() mapped every failure to DbError::Unreachable, so a wrong password told the operator to check a service that was running fine. SQLSTATE 28P01/28000 become AuthenticationFailed, 3D000 becomes DatabaseMissing, and Unreachable stays the fallback for genuine IO/DNS/timeout. Routed through a private function over &sqlx::Error so it is unit-testable without a live server.

nodes.label: redact_credentials
nodes.rationale: The only thing that may put a URL in an error message. Every new error variant must be covered by the regression test that classifies an error carrying postgres://lapidary:sup3rs3cret@db:5432/lapidary and asserts no rendered message contains the password — not just the variants that existed when the leak was found.

nodes.label: Prototype Knowledge Capture
nodes.rationale: Three of seven areas the spec required before deleting the Node prototype were missed: assetPipeline/meshSidecar ingest ordering, libraryScan's walk and debounce, and profileImport slicer profile parsing. Recoverable from origin/main, so not urgent — but slicer profile parsing is hard-won and heads for lapidary-targets, so capture it before that work starts. A finding that an area was thinner than claimed is a useful result, not a failure.
